title: Allotment or fiscal command?

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Mongol conquest and administrative subdivisions rather than a single uniform empire

objective: Mongol conquest and administrative subdivisions rather than a single uniform empire

claims.text: Samarkand fell to Chinggis Khan in 1220 with killing and forced displacement. Its region lay in Chagatai’s allotment, while fiscal administrators initially answered directly to the Great Khan.

claims.text: Samarkand’s conquest and a prince’s allotment did not put every office under the same authority. The accounts distinguish civil and fiscal reporting to the Great Khan from Kashgar’s later named administrators and madrasa. Under Alghu, civil administration shifted toward the ulus head. Conquest, allotment and reporting relationships therefore differ across time; the coercion of 1220 cannot become consent or a timeless uniform empire.
